newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 3.53 pct, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 3.53 pct, off highs.

text.p: Turkish shares continued their recovery following Tuesday's 8.76 percent plunge caused by heavy profit-taking, but afternoon selling erased part of the earlier gains, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 56 points, or 3.53 percent higher at 1,643 and compared to Monday's all-time high close of 1,700. It brushed a high of 1,696 in early trade and ended the first session at a new midday record of 1,683.
Trade volume rose sharply to 64.91 trillion lira ($560.2 million) from Wednesday's 48.52 trillion ($419 million) and neared Tuesday's 71.85 trillion lira ($619.4 million) record.
Brokers said resistance which emerged at the index's 1,700 level irritated the market slightly.

"The market met a stiff barrier at around 1,700 despite strong trade volumes recorded during the recent rally. Thus the index needs to regain its momentum before trying to overcome this barrier," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.
The index has recovered 5.93 percent since Tuesday's steep down correction which followed a 74.2 percent surge and 17 record closes from end-1996 to Monday's all-time high closing of 1,700.
The uptrend had speeded up after last Thursday's contitutional court ruling giving green light to Turk Telekom's sell-off.
